Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes. All my attempts to read the sources failed, so I have nothing verified to report.

**What went wrong:**
- I tried to open six pages: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub, and the NET Bible notes. The fetch tool turned every one down because I hadn't found those links through a search first.
- When I went back to run the searches, I had already used up my web tool calls for this turn. My other tools can't reach the internet.

You asked me not to fill gaps from memory, so I haven't written any verse notes. Notes without a page I'd actually read behind them could be wrong or credited to the wrong teacher.

**Next step:** if you ask again in a new message, I'll search before opening any pages, starting with these:
- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub or StudyLight
- **Tradition-specific views:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, Gill (Baptist), Ligonier and Monergism (Reformed), and LCMS or 1517 (Lutheran)
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent for Catholic and early Church Fathers material. I'll also check whether any of the allowed sites discuss Ezekiel 27 in relation to prosperity teaching.

Ezekiel 27 is mostly a poem about Tyre as a ship and a list of its trading partners. I expect few places where Protestant traditions really disagree, so that section may end up short or empty.
